info.title: Magic Lantern
info.description:
The HTTP API of the Magic Lantern daemon. Errors use one envelope: `{ error, message, issues? }`, where `error` is a stable kebab-case code.

Beyond the answers each operation lists, any request can get 500 `internal` (the cause is only in the daemon's log), and an unknown API route, or a documented path under a method it does not list, gets 404 `not-found` (never 405).

session.name: lantern_session
session.description: Set by `POST /api/v1/session`. In auth mode `password` every `/api/v1` route except `/api/v1/session` requires it; in mode `none` nothing does.

post.summary: Resolve a generation request without running it
post.description: The dry run: validates the request against the model's routes, chooses a route, fills every default by precedence (request > preset > model overrides > profile > route default), draws a seed for `"random"`, and reports what became of each field. A value the request sets is never changed: one the route can't take is a 422 whose issue may carry a `suggested` value.

additionalProperties.description: What became of one value (rule 4: no silent drops).

field.description: The field path in the request grammar (`sampling.steps`, `inputs.ref.weight`, `extensions.comfy`), for looking the field up in a descriptor.

state.description: `native`: the backend does it. `emulated`: Lantern does it around the backend. `ignored`: accepted, has no effect, and the field report says so. A field not listed at all is refused.

source.description: Where the value came from, by precedence (A3): `request`, then `preset`, `model` (the model's overrides), `profile`, `descriptor` (the route's default). `drawn`: a seed Lantern drew for `"random"`. `builtin`: Lantern's own fallback where nothing else gives one (`count` is 1).

requested.description: The value the request gave, when it gave one.

used.description: The value in `effective`. Absent when the route ignores the field.

reason.description: Why the field is emulated or ignored, for people.

route.description: The route a request resolved to.

health.description: A route's health and load state (L2).

status.description: Whether the route is reachable. Only `down` makes it unhealthy.

load_state.description: Whether the model is loaded. Not health (L2): a cold route under a manager loads on demand.

detail.description: More about the status, for people.

code.description: A stable code clients can key on, e.g. `negative_prompt_ignored`.

message.description: The advice, for people.

source.description: `profile`: one of the model profile's warnings. `resolver`: the resolver's own.

paths.description: The field paths the warning is about.

items.description: A route the resolver passed over before the one it chose. Routes ranked below the chosen one are not tried, so they are not listed.

reason.description: `down`: unreachable (a cold route is not skipped). `mode_unsupported`: the route does not serve the mode. `invalid`: the request does not validate on the route; `issues` says why.

issues.description: Present on `invalid`: pointers into the request.

path.description: The field at fault as a JSON pointer (RFC 6901, e.g. `/password`; `~` and `/` in a key are written `~0` and `~1`); for an unknown field, the pointer to that field; `''` for the whole body.

descriptor_digest.description: The digest of the route's effective descriptor, as `route_snapshot` keeps it.

provisional.description: Always true here: the route's health and the model's identity are checked again at dispatch (A12).

blocked_reason.description: Why a job could not be dispatched now; it stays queued (A12, L6).
